verdicts.what_i_ran: curl of https://openmrs.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/TRUNK-6701?fields=summary,description,status,comment - Requested change reads verbatim 'Only write session attributes when their values actually change, and remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute.'; status Closed; ibacher's comment records merge + 2.9.x/2.8.x/2.7.x backports. git grep -n INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID at d381957e = 2 hits (WebConstants.java:20 decl, OpenmrsFilter.java:64 write), zero readers; positive control git grep -ln OPENMRS_USER_CONTEXT_HTTPSESSION_ATTR = 3 files. gh api search/code q='INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID org:openmrs' = total_count 10. Fetched the two legacyui blobs via gh api repos/.../contents (raw.githubusercontent returned a 17-line error body, control grep 0 - exactly the failed-fetch trap; the gh api fetch gave 428 and 258 lines, control greps 1 and 1): PortletController.java:111-113 does an unguarded (String) getAttribute(...).equals(lastRequestId); HtmlIncludeTag.java:158-171 null-guards and log.errors. git diff eda229b1..d381957e hunks are RIGHT lines 10-16 and 72-97, so line 64 is outside the diff.
verdicts.refutation_attempted: Tried to break it four ways: (1) is the ticket really asking for two things - yes, verbatim; (2) is the PR actually incomplete against the definition of done - NO: the ticket's three Acceptance criteria bullets are entirely about session attributes ('same values as today', 'no writes when unchanged', 'tests cover both user states') and say nothing about the unique-id attribute, so the PR satisfies every acceptance criterion; (3) is the omission undocumented - only partly: OpenmrsFilter.java:63 already carries '// used by htmlInclude tag', which names the consumer; (4) is the ticket's premise false - no, 'nothing in core reads it' is literally true. What survived: the Requested-change prose does ask for a removal that would NPE legacyui's PortletController, and the ticket is Closed.
verdicts.why: The observation (half the Requested change shipped, removal would break legacyui) holds, but its stated ask is wrong: the ticket's premise 'nothing in core reads it' is literally true and needs no correcting, and line 63's existing comment already names the consumer. Anchors at line 64, which this diff does not touch.

verdicts.what_i_ran: Census: python scan of every git-tracked *.xml under a */src/test/resources path for a <dataset> root element -> 1 at a resources root (web/src/test/resources/OpenmrsFilterTest-initial.xml) vs 122 under package paths (positive control that the scan finds pre-existing datasets). The other root-level xml files are log4j2.xml, TestingApplicationContext.xml, AltAuthSchemeTestingApplicationContext.xml, override-web.xml - all classpath-root by necessity. executeDataSet(String) at BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:685-706 resolves via getClass().getClassLoader().getResourceAsStream, so any package path works. mvn -o -pl web help:effective-pom: maven-jar-plugin appears in effective build/plugins (declared at pom.xml:527-530, inheriting the pluginManagement execution at pom.xml:117-136) with goals jar AND test-jar; web/target/test-classes/OpenmrsFilterTest-initial.xml is at the root; test-suite/module/omod/pom.xml depends on org.openmrs.web:openmrs-web type test-jar. The only other executeDataSet in the web module (UpdateFilterTest.java:45) uses a package path.
verdicts.refutation_attempted: Tried to break it three ways: (1) is the plugin config only pluginManagement (which would make the tests.jar claim wrong)? - no, openmrs-web really does inherit the test-jar execution, effective-pom confirms; (2) is there precedent for a root-level test resource in web? - yes, but both are root-by-necessity (log4j2 auto-discovery, a classpath*: spring context), which a DBUnit dataset is not; (3) does the bare name actually collide with anything today? - no, the name is unique across both test-jars, so this is hygiene, not breakage. The convention claim survived.
verdicts.why: Verified exactly as stated. It is a convention/hygiene finding with no live failure, and it is moot if the fixture is deleted per F01/F11/F17.

verdicts.what_i_ran: Probe printed defaultLocale=[en_GB], equalsENGLISH=false, and the filter wrote a java.util.Locale (en_GB) into the session. Mutation C: changed line 193's seed from Locale.ENGLISH to Locale.UK (= en_GB, the ambient default) -> mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest fails with exactly 'org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: expected: <1> but was: <0>' at OpenmrsFilterTest.java:214 - the predicted failure. Traced the source of en_GB: no default_locale row exists anywhere in api/ or web/ test resources, so LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale() falls back to OpenmrsConstants.GLOBAL_PROPERTY_DEFAULT_LOCALE_DEFAULT_VALUE = 'en_GB' (OpenmrsConstants.java:326).
verdicts.refutation_attempted: Tried to break it by (a) checking whether the seed is pinned by something in the test (it is not - it is a bare literal), and (b) checking whether the value it is coupled to is volatile. (b) partly bites: the coupling is to a hardcoded core constant, not to a GP row that exists in the baseline, so the stated trigger requires someone to add a default_locale GP. The mechanism itself reproduced exactly, so the finding stands.
verdicts.why: Reproduced the predicted failure verbatim. Slight imprecision: the ambient default comes from the GLOBAL_PROPERTY_DEFAULT_LOCALE_DEFAULT_VALUE constant, not from a default_locale GP in the test dataset, which makes the trigger more remote than the wording suggests - hence nit, as the finding itself says.

verdicts.what_i_ran: git grep '"locale"' -- web/src/main = 3 hits: OpenmrsFilter.java:94 (the rewritten line), FilterUtil.java:36 (the constant declaration) and a .vm template. git grep LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE -- web/src/main = 29 uses, all via FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE, in StartupFilter, InitializationFilter and UpdateFilter. Probe confirmed the type divergence empirically: PROBE_SESSIONLOCALE=[en_GB] class=java.util.Locale from OpenmrsFilter, while InitializationFilter.java:1019 writes locale.toString(). Follow-up check on the suggested fix: FilterUtil has no constant for the sibling 'username' session key (ADMIN_USERNAME = "admin" is a username value, not an attribute key), and its class javadoc scopes it to "admin's user property and ... default locale property" - it is the startup-wizard helper. The new test class itself declares private local USERNAME_ATTRIBUTE/LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE constants rather than importing FilterUtil's.
verdicts.refutation_attempted: Tried to break it: (1) pre-existing? the literal is, but the PR rewrote that exact line, so it is in scope; (2) is the suggested fix actually right? this is the strongest counter - FilterUtil is the startup-wizard helper and its LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE denotes a String-typed slot, so adopting it asserts a shared contract that is in fact type-divergent; (3) is it symmetric? no - the 'username' literal on line 93 has no constant, so only half the line can be constant-ised. Neither counter falsifies the observation. The follow-up check strengthened counter (2) and added counter (3): the suggested edit would make the two adjacent keys inconsistent and would couple the main request filter to the startup-wizard utility class. The observation still stands; its value does not.
verdicts.why: The observation is true - line 94 is the only bare "locale" left in web/src/main while 29 other uses go through FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE - but 'this module already exports a constant for it' oversells the fix. Three independent counters: the constant belongs to the startup-wizard helper and denotes a String-typed slot (the finding supplies this one itself); the sibling "username" on line 93 has no constant, so applying it leaves the pair inconsistent; and the PR's own test class chose local constants over importing FilterUtil's. Also 'two other filters in the same package' is loose - they are in the .initialization and .update sub-packages.

verdicts.what_i_ran: Serialization probe (ZzSerProbeTest, since deleted) under BaseWebContextSensitiveTest: 'SER_PROBE userContext instanceof Serializable = true' but 'SER_PROBE RESULT=FAILED java.io.NotSerializableException: org.openmrs.api.context.TestUsernameAuthenticationScheme' - and the same for a freshly constructed UserContext, exactly as OpenmrsFilter builds one. Source confirms this is not a test artefact: UserContext.java declares a non-transient 'private final AuthenticationScheme authenticationScheme', AuthenticationScheme is a plain interface, DaoAuthenticationScheme implements it without Serializable, and the production UsernamePasswordAuthenticationScheme extends DaoAuthenticationScheme. Also checked for a core listener that depended on the per-request writes: git grep HttpSessionAttributeListener/attributeReplaced/attributeAdded = zero hits (positive control: HttpSessionListener finds web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java).
verdicts.refutation_attempted: I set out to confirm this one and instead broke it. The removal of incidental dirty-marking is real (the PR's own shouldNotRewriteUnchanged* tests assert zero writes on a steady-state request). But the stated consequence cannot occur: any session store that persists or replicates must serialize the session, and serializing this UserContext throws NotSerializableException on its authenticationScheme field, so the in-place mutations to roles/privileges/location were never persisted or replicated before this PR either. The finding's own counter-evidence already concedes the other half (per-attribute delta managers only ever replicated the username/locale keys, never the userContext key). That leaves no store for which the consequence holds.
verdicts.why: True observation, refuted failure mode: UserContext is unserializable in practice, so the authorization state this finding worries about was never replicated. The question has no answer that would change the code.

verdicts.what_i_ran: Mutation A, applied myself: replaced the two setSessionAttributeIfChanged calls at OpenmrsFilter.java:93-94 with a single guard keyed only on the username - if (!Objects.equals(httpSession.getAttribute("username"), username)) { setAttribute username; setAttribute locale; } -> mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest = 'Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0'. The mutant survives. Reachability of the scenario confirmed in tree: UserContext.getLocale() returns LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale() uncached for an anonymous context, and Context.setLocale(Locale) (Context.java:880) delegates to UserContext.setLocale for a mid-session language switch on an unchanged username. Production file restored with git checkout --; git status --porcelain clean.
verdicts.refutation_attempted: Tried to break it: (1) is some other test in the class sensitive to the mutant? - all five move username and locale together, so none is; (2) is the locale-only scenario actually unreachable, which would make the gap moot? - no, Context.setLocale is the public mid-session locale switch and getLocale() re-reads the default for anonymous contexts; (3) would a cheaper assertion already cover it? - no, every countWrites assertion in the class is symmetric across the two keys. The mutant survived every attempt to kill it.
verdicts.why: Reproduced independently: a single username-keyed guard passes the whole class, so the suite does not pin the locale guard as independent - which is precisely the behaviour TRUNK-6701 was filed about.

most_serious_defect_in_this_pr: A test-coverage hole that leaves the ticket's own motivating behaviour unpinned. All five tests move the username and the locale in lockstep, so nothing in the suite distinguishes two independent guards from one. I replaced both setSessionAttributeIfChanged calls with a single guard keyed only on the username and the class still went 5/5 green - meaning a later refactor could reintroduce exactly the redundant per-request locale write that TRUNK-6701 was filed to remove (and, worse, could suppress a legitimate locale write after Context.setLocale on an authenticated session, so the servlet container's view of the session locale would go stale) without any test noticing. Everything else in this PR is cosmetic: the production change is behaviourally equivalent to the base for both anonymous and authenticated requests, and I found no way to make it misbehave.
